newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM Klaus says no cabinet changes imminent.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM Klaus says no cabinet changes imminent.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Thursday ruled out any imminent government reshuffle, rejecting calls for change over the worsening state of the economy.
"It is not a question for the immediately following period," Klaus told a news conference. "We are not considering a trivial restructuring which would be a simple exchange (of ministers)."

The government announced on Wednesday a sweeping series of measures to boost the economy, including deep cuts in public spending, limits on public sector wage growth and an acceleration in privatisation.

"It is correct that the credibility of the measures, (if) supported by personnel shifts in the cabinet, would be greater," Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec of Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) told CTK news agency.
Klaus said the government was considering a longer-term change in the spheres of responsibility of ministries.
"Together with that we would do not only restructuring of the cabinet but also a personnel exchange," he said.

The government is a three-party coalition dominated by the ODS. Tensions have increased in the coalition since last June's parliamentary election at which it lost its majority. It has since regained a majority through opposition defections.
